fixes.explanation: That's the line, friend. The LORD says to David's Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.” (Psalm 110:1) Notice He says sit. The footstool is the part the LORD says He will make.

A tent? I looked all through this psalm, friend, and I couldn't find so much as a tent peg. The LORD extends the scepter from Zion and says, “Rule in the midst of Your enemies.” (Psalm 110:2) That's a command to rule, not to go back and wait.

Right, and that's the whole point of the line. David says, “Your people shall be willing on Your day of battle.” (Psalm 110:3) Willing is the word he uses. Though I will say a plate of cookies never hurt anybody's attendance.

Priest it is. The LORD swears, “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.” (Psalm 110:4) The verse says the LORD has sworn and will not change His mind. That oath is what the word forever stands on, friend.
Shepherd is a lovely word, friend. But in this verse the LORD swears, “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.” (Psalm 110:4). The word He swears is priest.
Giants make a good story, friend. But here David says, “He will crush kings in the day of His wrath.” (Psalm 110:5). The psalm names kings, and giants aren't in it. It's a heavy verse, friend.
Shepherds are fine, friend. But this verse says, “He will crush kings in the day of His wrath.” (Psalm 110:5). The psalm names kings, and shepherds don't show up here.

That's right. David says of Him, “He will judge the nations, heaping up the dead…” (Psalm 110:6). Look back at verse 5 and you'll see it's about the same One who crushes kings. Now that One judges the nations, friend.

This one's true, friend. Verse 5 says He will crush kings in the day of His wrath, and verse 6 goes on with “He will judge the nations, heaping up the dead…” (Psalm 110:6). It's one picture with one Person doing it.
